independent.summary: checkApp reports `status: asset.status` (0) when only the hashed-bundle probe transport-fails, even though the app page itself answered 200; since 'app' is a single-check host, collectability then calls the host unreachable and --baseline exits 2, blocking the whole night on a reached-but-partially-failing Netlify — exactly the default-deny outcome the item exists to avoid (and the detail string reads 'which answers 0').

classify() refuses a baseline with collected:false but never looks at `after.collected`, which runSmoke now computes: if production is unreachable at compare time every green check reads as a regression, so a DNS/network fault on the runner side triggers autoRevert of a healthy merge — the mirror of the hole just closed on the baseline side, with the data to detect it already in hand.

triageGrades.reason: No authentication or authorization logic is added or changed; the pre-existing X-API-Key headers are untouched.
No credentials are added, logged, or moved — the new debug lines print URLs, statuses and transport errors only.
The paid /chat probe is unchanged; nothing in the diff alters billing, pricing, or spend.
The only write is the pre-existing baseline file write; no deletes or irreversible operations are introduced.
Right that the change touches outbound HTTP handling — probe() is modified and collectability() reinterprets probe results — even though line 144 is weak evidence.
Wrong: this is the nightly deploy gate — the diff adds a new blocking exit 2, a --compare refusal, and rewrites the RUNBOOK's deploy/block procedure, so release gating is squarely touched.

summary: The local review found nothing at all, missing both the single-check 'app' host misclassification and the unused after.collected on the compare path, and its triage was right on five of six categories while calling the deploy-gate change not release-related.
